messages:
incident-bot: [P1] Verdant Health (VPC) — auth errors spike: OIDC token validation failing for inbound requests to tenant bridge. Alerting 3xx failures in front of dedicated pool. Pager: ops-oncall. (auto-detected at 2026-03-15T09:12:58Z)

ops-oncall: saw the page, I'm taking it. status: investigating. Assigning to alice and ben.

alice.nguyen: jumping in. verdant reported 502s and 401s after their weekend key rotation. they said they rotated keys at ~08:50 UTC.

ben.kline: can we confirm JWKS fetches? fetching the tenant JWKS now from the bridge: `curl -s -D - https://verdant-tenant.example/.well-known/jwks.json` — getting 200 but keys array empty. (reaction :eyes:)

chao.li: if JWKS is empty the local JWKS cache might fall through. our AuthN path rejects tokens when no matching kid found. adding logs:```
Mar 15 09:12:35 auth-bridge[pid:4221] WARN no-jwk-for-kid kid=abcd1234 token_id=xyz request_id=req-7f2e
Mar 15 09:12:36 proxy[pid:110] ERROR upstream 502 tenant=verdant route=bridge-01
```

cassie.sr: tagging customer-success; I already pinged Verdant SRE — they said their rotation hit production but their key publish job failed intermittently. They're working on re-publishing.

alice.nguyen: quick mitigation idea: route Verdant's auth requests to the fallback keystore that contains previous key material for 15m while they republish. Ops, can we flip a temporary policy?

devops-bot: rollback-policy executed: set-policy verdant-bridge allow-fallback-keystore=true duration=15m (initiated by alice.nguyen)

ben.kline: applied change, waiting for propagation to all bridge instances. Confirming with a quick curl to auth endpoint.```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{ "status": "ok", "subject": "user:alice@verdant" }
```

ops-oncall: traffic looks healthy now, 401s dropped from 80% -> 2% in the last 2m. tagging incident as mitigated but still P1 until root cause and customer is fully back.

pm-elaine: escalate note for execs: Verdant impacted, production requests degraded for ~22m. We're using fallback keystore; customer is re-publishing keys. Will follow up with RCA. (reaction :page_with_curl:)

chao.li: root cause hypothesis: Verdant's rotation job replaced key material but published an empty JWKS on the public endpoint due to a bug in their republishing script — our tenant bridge didn't cache the previous JWKS long enough and strict kid verification caused mass auth rejections.

alice.nguyen: long-term actions: (1) extend local JWKS cache TTL to 30m for tenant bridges, (2) add a validation check in our provisioning that rejects publish with empty jwks array, (3) surface explicit health signal when a tenant's JWKS is malformed. I'll open tickets.

ben.kline: created infra ticket INF-4521: "Extend tenant JWKS cache and add malformed-jwks guard". Assigned to eng-platform.

cassie.sr: customer update sent: "We've enabled a temporary fallback on your bridge to accept recently rotated keys while you re-publish. Please verify that your JWKS endpoint returns the new keys and confirm so we can remove the fallback." Verdant replied: "republishing now, will confirm in ~5m"

ops-oncall: once Verdant confirms, we'll rotate back to strict mode and close. leaving notes for postmortem: timeline, mitigation commands, who was paged, and customer communications.

incident-bot: Incident status changed: P1 -> mitigated (temporary fallback applied). Incident channel: #incidents. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/vpc-oidc (admin only).
summary: P1 - Verdant Health VPC OIDC auth failures after customer key rotation; temporary fallback keystore applied; cache TTL and publish validation planned
